fields.RequiredArtifact: Selected V1 branch: **Branch B**. **Branch A:** a public AI Party type and an authorization contract permitting only the Agents Service Principal to create `hexa`'s deterministic provisioned Party under that type. **Branch B:** Parties Maintainer and Product formally accept the existing Organization-typed provisioned Party as the V1 launch contract, verified everywhere by its immutable deterministic id and never by type. Both branches require create-only AD-2 provisioning, idempotent exact retries, typed conflict for divergent identity/type requests, mandatory tenant scope, no tenant-role creation or replacement, and no Party PII in public results. The record must name the selected branch; absence of that decision is `Uncommitted`. Independently of the selected identity branch, Parties exposes a tenant-scoped authoritative resolution by `PartyId` returning stable Party classification (`Human`, `Organization`, or `AI`), active/liveness state, evidence position and observed instant, plus typed missing, ambiguous, stale, denied, and unavailable outcomes. For every human Party, the same seam also returns one stable non-PII `AuthenticatedHumanActorId`, `HumanActorBindingVersion`, validity interval, and queryable binding history sufficient to reproduce the identity in force at an action; it returns typed missing, ambiguous, stale, and overlapping-history outcomes. AD-8 uses both classification and binding at predefined-approver configuration and every runtime approver resolution; non-human Parties can never be Approvers, and a human command carrying a Party must bind to the same authenticated actor id.

fields.RequiredArtifact: Six core V1 seams. (1) Membership: public `IConversationClient.AddParticipantAsync` and `POST /api/v1/conversations/{conversationId}/participants`, limited for Agents to stable AI Party identity, `ParticipantType.AiAgent`, and `ParticipantRole.Member`; exact retries are idempotent no-ops, conflicting type/role is a typed conflict, and cross-tenant or general participant management is denied; plus a participant-state read for the AI participant and a participant removal limited to the AI participant for the PRD FR-2 removal block. Before accepting membership, Conversations verifies the immutable provisioned Party by id and additionally verifies AI type only when `EXT-PARTIES-1` commits Branch A; Branch B accepts its approved Organization type by id; the record owner supplies the final member and typed failure names (A-21). (2) Posting: append a Conversation Message as the `AiAgent` participant with an Agents-supplied deterministic `MessageId` and idempotency key, persisted verbatim or rejected (a differing returned id is a typed incompatibility that blocks posting), and message metadata carrying the Agent Call trace reference and provenance flags (AI-generated; human-edited and by which Party), so restart or replay cannot duplicate a post; plus an existence read by `MessageId` returning the message, typed absence, typed `ConversationDeleted`, typed `PrincipalRemovedFromConversation`, or unavailable, so Agents can check before retry or abandonment after a lost acknowledgement and record `LateConfirmed` rather than contradict an already-posted message. (3) Facilitator resolution: `ParticipantRole.Facilitator` on the participant read model. (4) The Eligible Conversation denominator is supplied either as an active-Conversation count per tenant/window or as a Conversations-side tenant event feed from which Agents computes the same count, never from Agent Calls (A-4). (5) Tenant-scoped reads under the Agents Service Principal of complete Conversation content, the Participant roster with roles, and Conversation existence/accessibility; they return typed `ConversationDeleted` and `PrincipalRemovedFromConversation` distinctly from transient denial or error, and content contains the messages a Participant would currently see, including current edit/delete state (A-15). (6) A Conversations-owned durable outbox or ordered tenant/source feed entry created atomically with the approved Conversation-deletion decision. It carries one immutable `ConversationDeletionSignalId` bound one-to-one to that logical approval, `TenantId`, `ConversationId`, stable source stream/revision, approval reference, source-contract version, and an independent delivery-attempt id. Reconnect/backfill is ordered from a durable checkpoint; the source retains and retries the same logical entry through Agents outage, typed refusal, target-version rollover, and lost acknowledgement until authenticated `DeletionSignalAccepted(SignalId, SourceRevision, ProtectedDeletionRevision)` advances the checkpoint. Retransmission never mints a new signal id/source revision; changed fields at the same id are a quarantined compatibility conflict that is not skipped or acknowledged, blocks seam readiness, and exposes only safe poison metadata. Source-revision and Agents acknowledgement lookup resolve both sides of lost delivery. The authenticated source identity and exact target are verified before Agents dispatch; the signal triggers PRD FR-30 deletion of derived Agent content and never grants a human Agents role, local cancellation authority, or scope beyond that source Conversation. Final member and typed failure names are owned by this record (PRD §8.1 assumptions A-1 through A-4, A-15, A-16, A-21).

fieldsUnchanged.Owner: Project owner (user declaration 2026-10-07), acting as Conversations Maintainer
fieldsUnchanged.RequiredArtifact: Six core V1 seams. (1) Membership: public `IConversationClient.AddParticipantAsync` and `POST /api/v1/conversations/{conversationId}/participants`, limited for Agents to stable AI Party identity, `ParticipantType.AiAgent`, and `ParticipantRole.Member`; exact retries are idempotent no-ops, conflicting type/role is a typed conflict, and cross-tenant or general participant management is denied; plus a participant-state read for the AI participant and a participant removal limited to the AI participant for the PRD FR-2 removal block. Before accepting membership, Conversations verifies the immutable provisioned Party by id and additionally verifies AI type only when `EXT-PARTIES-1` commits Branch A; Branch B accepts its approved Organization type by id; the record owner supplies the final member and typed failure names (A-21). (2) Posting: append a Conversation Message as the `AiAgent` participant with an Agents-supplied deterministic `MessageId` and idempotency key, persisted verbatim or rejected (a differing returned id is a typed incompatibility that blocks posting), and message metadata carrying the Agent Call trace reference and provenance flags (AI-generated; human-edited and by which Party), so restart or replay cannot duplicate a post; plus an existence read by `MessageId` returning the message, typed absence, typed `ConversationDeleted`, typed `PrincipalRemovedFromConversation`, or unavailable, so Agents can check before retry or abandonment after a lost acknowledgement and record `LateConfirmed` rather than contradict an already-posted message. (3) Facilitator resolution: `ParticipantRole.Facilitator` on the participant read model. (4) The Eligible Conversation denominator is supplied either as an active-Conversation count per tenant/window or as a Conversations-side tenant event feed from which Agents computes the same count, never from Agent Calls (A-4). (5) Tenant-scoped reads under the Agents Service Principal of complete Conversation content, the Participant roster with roles, and Conversation existence/accessibility; they return typed `ConversationDeleted` and `PrincipalRemovedFromConversation` distinctly from transient denial or error, and content contains the messages a Participant would currently see, including current edit/delete state (A-15). (6) A Conversations-owned durable outbox or ordered tenant/source feed entry created atomically with the approved Conversation-deletion decision. It carries one immutable `ConversationDeletionSignalId` bound one-to-one to that logical approval, `TenantId`, `ConversationId`, stable source stream/revision, approval reference, source-contract version, and an independent delivery-attempt id. Reconnect/backfill is ordered from a durable checkpoint; the source retains and retries the same logical entry through Agents outage, typed refusal, target-version rollover, and lost acknowledgement until authenticated `DeletionSignalAccepted(SignalId, SourceRevision, ProtectedDeletionRevision)` advances the checkpoint. Retransmission never mints a new signal id/source revision; changed fields at the same id are a quarantined compatibility conflict that is not skipped or acknowledged, blocks seam readiness, and exposes only safe poison metadata. Source-revision and Agents acknowledgement lookup resolve both sides of lost delivery. The authenticated source identity and exact target are verified before Agents dispatch; the signal triggers PRD FR-30 deletion of derived Agent content and never grants a human Agents role, local cancellation authority, or scope beyond that source Conversation. Final member and typed failure names are owned by this record (PRD §8.1 assumptions A-1 through A-4, A-15, A-16, A-21).
fieldsUnchanged.CompatibilityContractAndVerificationComm: Contract: typed idempotent membership with participant-state read, AI-participant removal, and Hexalith.Parties identity-by-id verification plus AI-type verification only under committed Branch A; idempotent posting with trace/provenance metadata and a typed `MessageId` existence read covering message, absence, deletion, principal removal, and unavailable; Facilitator role exposure; active-Conversation count or equivalent Conversations-side tenant event feed; tenant-scoped current content/roster/existence/accessibility reads that distinguish deletion/removal from transient denial/error; and atomic durable approved-deletion outbox/feed delivery with stable logical signal/source revision, ordered checkpoint/backfill, retry until authenticated Agents acknowledgement, target-version rollover, conflict quarantine/no-skip, acknowledgement/source lookup, local-cancellation denial, and focused cross-tenant denial. During owner qualification the receiver role is filled per accepted cohort `OQ-5.4-1` item 1.
